ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A bare-handed thief is a thief who takes openly without needing tools or concealment.
EvidenceBody: Chan verses warn people to watch for the bare-handed thief, call a captured figure one, or praise the thief’s skill. Quan’an says even a hall full of gold and jade must watch for him; other records speak of exposed stolen goods. Praise and accusation both occur.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The thief becomes a Chan epithet and warning inside appraisals of taking, capture, and exposed goods.
